tools.name: publish
tools.description: Publish HTML or Markdown as a hosted web page and return a shareable URL. Use when the user asks to share an HTML quiz, calculator, report or Markdown document as a link. HTML JavaScript runs in a sandbox. Free links expire after seven days; paid link lifetime and options follow account entitlements

tools.name: list_my_pages
tools.description: List the pages you have published to dochost, newest first. Paginated; returns compact records (no page bodies).

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Get your plan, page-quota usage, entitlement flags (size cap, custom slug, password, branding, subdomain, custom domain), and the primary host new links publish on. Call when you need plan limits, domain details or paid-option availability; a basic publish can use defaults without this extra call. T

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Get one of your pages by slug: title, format, status, view/like counts, expiry, whether it is password-protected, and its current visibility / indexing / branding state. Never returns the page body or the password — call get_page_content when you need the source itself, and set_page_options to chang

tools.name: get_page_content
tools.description: Read back the CURRENT Markdown or HTML of one of your pages. Call this before update_page whenever you did not write the live content yourself in this same conversation — update_page replaces the body wholesale, so editing from memory silently discards anything you cannot see, including edits the us

tools.name: update_page
tools.description: Replace the content of one of your pages in place. The URL, view/like counts, and expiry stay the same; only the body, format, and title change. Resending identical content is a no-op. Prefer this over publishing again whenever the user is revising something you already published for them — a second

tools.description: Change a published page's visibility, search-engine indexing or password WITHOUT republishing it — the URL, view count and content all stay the same. tools.name: delete_page
tools.description: Permanently delete one of your pages by slug. The link stops working immediately and the slug is freed. Deleting an already-deleted page is a safe no-op.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_page_content, update_page, set_page_options · Private data: publish, list_my_pages, get_account, get_page, set_page_options · Public sink: publish, get_account, update_page, set_page_options · Destructive: get_page, update_page, delete_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_page_content, update_page, set_page_options · Private data: publish, list_my_pages, get_account, get_page, set_page_options · Public sink: publish, get_account, update_page, set_page_options · Destructive: get_page, update_page, delete_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "publish" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
